hints: Recall that speed is a scalar magnitude, so after collision $Q$ moves forward with velocity $+v$, while $P$ can move forward ($+v$) or rebound backwards ($-v$).
Apply the principle of conservation of linear momentum: $m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$, with initial momentum $0.1(4) = 0.4\text{ N s}$.
walkthrough:
Name the foundational principle: on a smooth horizontal plane with no external forces, linear momentum is conserved in the collision:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$

Calculate the total initial momentum before impact:
$$p_i = (0.1)(4) + (0.4)(0) = 0.4\text{ N s}$$
After the collision, both particles have the same speed $v$. Because particle $Q$ is struck from behind, it must move forward in the positive direction ($v_Q = +v$).
Particle $P$ can either continue forwards ($v_P = +v$) or rebound backwards ($v_P = -v$).

Case 1: Particle $P$ continues forward in the original direction ($v_P = +v$):
$$0.1v + 0.4v = 0.4$$
$$0.5v = 0.4$$
$$v = \frac{0.4}{0.5} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Case 2: Particle $P$ reverses direction upon impact ($v_P = -v$):
$$-0.1v + 0.4v = 0.4$$
$$0.3v = 0.4$$
$$v = \frac{0.4}{0.3} = \frac{4}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}\quad (\approx 1.33\text{ m s}^{-1})$$
